title: UPDATE: Cloudflare Integrates Pi Durable Into Agents SDK v0.26.0

tickers.name: Cloudflare, Inc. Class A common stock, par value $0.001 per share

summary:
The persistence layer provided by Pi Durable is now operational on Cloudflare Durable Objects following a series of technical updates to the company's agent tooling. The integration, delivered in version 0.26.0 of the agents SDK, allows developers to install the runtime via the npm package manager to maintain state for autonomous AI agents on the network's infrastructure.

The release accompanies the Oct. 1 launch of Pi 1.0, a customizable coding harness for AI agents. This version introduces 'codemode,' which enables agents to write scripts to orchestrate tool calls and filter data outside the model's context to reduce latency and token costs. Industry developers have noted that durable runtimes are becoming a necessary requirement for all agent harnesses.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Builders need coding agents and harnesses to be more malleable
selectedTweets.text:
Learn to build a custom harness, folks. 

Mods in Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness, and now Pi Durable.

What do these all have in common?

Increased extensibility.

Builders need coding agents and harnesses to be more malleable. 

Say you are building a simple agentic app for your users, a personalized headless experience,  a software factory, or a domain-specific harness; you will quickly find that the generic harness won't cut it. Sometimes you need a different behavior in the UI. Sometimes you just need to easily add a new feature/plugin. Or sometimes you just want to build a completely new experience, like multiplayer support. 

You can build it from scratch, as I recommend. I mean, it's not that hard. But if you want to hit the ground running, where do you go? Pi Durable and DeepSeek Harness seem to want to solve that problem.

Users want more customization in their harnesses. And those builders who understand how to build and maintain one will win big time from this next phase of more malleable harnesses. 

The battle of the best harness will be very different from the first wave of generic harnesses.

selectedTweets.bestBit: codemode lets the agent write a script that orchestrates those calls, filters and combines the data, and returns the relevant result
selectedTweets.text:
An agent can fill its context with tool output before it gets to the useful part.

Imagine checking tons of issues and PRs plus their comments. With individual tool calls, the model repeatedly receives raw results just to decide what to fetch or filter next.

codemode lets the agent write a script that orchestrates those calls, filters and combines the data, and returns the relevant result. Independent calls can run in parallel. Intermediate data can stay outside the model’s context.

The tools still do the work, but fewer steps need a model round trip. That can reduce latency and token costs while leaving more context for reasoning.

Pi Agent 1.0 is the latest example, adding codemode alongside deferred tool loading.

I use @pidotdev as my daily driver. Its adoption is a useful example of harnesses evolving with both user needs and model capabilities: giving agents better ways to compose tools as workflows grow longer.
